name: Fashion collection development and launch
one_line: A purpose-coherent fashion collection moving from concept and design development through samples, line-sheet communication, production readiness, and launch; an isolated garment image, moodboard, or brand guide is not enough.

deterministic: A collection packet with a named season or drop, collection concept, coordinated style or look identifiers, and multiple garment design records; the repeated collection identifier across members is stronger than a fashion word in one filename.

Development evidence spanning at least two lifecycle roles: garment sketches or flats plus a tech pack, fit/sample review, line sheet, production order, or launch asset, with matching style identifiers or collection language.
A line sheet or wholesale assortment document that maps style numbers to garment names, colourways, sizes, prices or order information and is explicitly tied to a collection or season.
A production-ready packet containing graded specifications, bill of materials, measurement tables, construction details, sample comments, and factory or delivery instructions for coordinated styles.
A collection launch packet whose lookbook, campaign selects, product copy, and assortment or release plan share a collection/drop identity and refer back to developed styles.
needs_llm: deciding whether a set of garments is a coherent collection or merely a designer portfolio, retail assortment, costume wardrobe, or reference board; the model must cite collection-level language and cross-file style evidence
resolving lifecycle role when a file says sample, proto, salesman sample, production, or launch without a readable style identifier or collection anchor
separating an internal collection packet from a client engagement deliverable, a brand identity guide, a portfolio case study, or a licensed product reference
deciding whether an archive is one collection packet when member filenames are heterogeneous but its manifest, repeated style codes, and season/drop references establish a shared workflow
never_alone: the words fashion, apparel, collection, capsule, runway, resort, couture, lookbook, season, spring, summer, fall, winter, drop, garment, dress, jacket, or sample alone
a season or year alone, a style number alone, a SKU alone, or a bare size/colour token
a garment photograph, runway photograph, sketch, flat, pattern, CAD file, fabric swatch, or mannequin image alone
a brand, designer, factory, retailer, buyer, model, or celebrity name alone; names can be subjects, counterparties, references, or issuers
a parent folder named Collection, SS26, Fashion, Samples, Production, or Launch, a download session, or shared-drive membership
FINAL, APPROVED, SAMPLE, FIT, PROTO, DROP, or version suffixes without collection-level and lifecycle evidence
a public lookbook, trend report, fashion show image, or downloaded product catalogue without evidence it belongs to the holder's own collection workflow

grouping_reasons: one collection or drop across concept, style development, materials, samples, line sheet, production, and launch materials
one garment style across its sketch, tech pack, pattern, sample comments, approved specification, and production record when identifiers and revisions agree
one release or assortment packet when the line sheet, lookbook, product copy, and launch plan share a collection identity
no collection group for an isolated fashion image, generic trend board, public reference catalogue, or one garment file without collection-level evidence

template.why: Empty by binding contract: the creative schema currently declares no fields. The lifecycle is a template situation, not permission to mint collection, season, garment, or stage fields here. If the shared creative schema later gains destination-eligible fields, collection or project context should precede lifecycle/artifact values so a terminal work type such as a fit comment or line sheet remains intelligible; this is not time-first because season and launch dates describe the collection's chronology rather than replacing its identity.

collides_with.signal: A curated lookbook or runway image can be a portfolio work sample rather than an active collection record. Collection identifiers plus development, production, or assortment evidence support this template; capability framing, selected-work narrative, and audience-facing case-study structure support the career template.

Fashion photographs and lookbook selects may be camera captures or authored launch assets. Camera-origin and event chronology support photos; style identifiers and collection lifecycle evidence support this template. Appearance alone is not discriminating.

A fashion label's brand manual and a collection launch packet may share a brand name and visual assets. Governed marks, identity rules, and permitted-use guidance support brand identity; garment development, assortment, and production evidence support this template.

A commissioned collection may contain a brief, schedule, and deliverables alongside design and production files. Scope, counterparties, fees, and review obligations support client engagement; the collection's garment lifecycle and assortment evidence support this template.

falls_through_to.why: A readable line sheet, tech pack, or production notice with no supported collection group remains a durable standalone record.
Sparse style files, detached sample comments, and mixed archives need review before collection facts are accepted.
Public trend reports, downloaded lookbooks, and fashion references without holder-owned development evidence are reading or reference material.
An isolated garment or runway image without collection evidence is not a collection situation.
Screenshots of seller portals, fit chats, or launch dashboards remain screenshot material unless their own evidence supports the collection packet.
Unreadable proprietary pattern or CAD archives remain indexed without forced inspection.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased designs, technical specifications, factory terms, buyer pricing, launch timing, model images, and licensed fabrics or marks may expose commercial strategy or third-party rights. Protection follows the evidence and rights record, not fashion words or extensions.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: when the creative schema is ratified, decide whether collection/project, lifecycle stage, artifact type, and season/drop are shared canonical fields or whether season remains a value/search facet. Also decide whether a commissioned fashion collection should co-activate this template and creative.client-engagement on disjoint role evidence, or whether client engagement remains the sole activation with this as a later group subtype. No field is proposed here because the current creative schema is intentionally empty.
